title: What Earth in 2050 could look like - Shannon Odell

blocks.en_text: While we’re already feeling the devastating effects
blocks.zh_text: 虽然我们已经感受到毁灭性的影响

blocks.en_text: of human-caused climate change,
blocks.zh_text: 来自人类造成的气候变化，

blocks.en_text: governments continue to fall short on making and executing emissions pledges
blocks.zh_text: 但各国政府在制定和执行减排承诺上仍然做得不够

blocks.en_text: that would help thwart further warming.
blocks.zh_text: 而这些承诺本可以帮助阻止进一步变暖。

blocks.en_text: So, what will our world look like in the next 30 to 80 years,
blocks.zh_text: 那么，我们的世界在未来30到80年会是什么样子，

blocks.en_text: if we continue on the current path?
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们继续沿着现在的路走下去？

blocks.en_text: While it’s impossible to know exactly how the next decade will unfold,
blocks.zh_text: 虽然我们无法确切知道下一个十年会如何发展，

blocks.en_text: scientists and climate experts have made projections,
blocks.zh_text: 但科学家和气候专家已经做出了预测，

blocks.en_text: factoring in the current state of affairs.
blocks.zh_text: 把当前的状况考虑了进去。

blocks.en_text: This future we’re about to describe is bleak,
blocks.zh_text: 我们即将描述的这个未来是黯淡的，

blocks.en_text: but remember there’s still time to ensure it doesn’t become our reality.
blocks.zh_text: 但请记住，我们仍有时间确保它不会成为现实。
现在是2050年。

blocks.en_text: We’ve blown past the 1.5 degree target that world leaders promised to stick to.
blocks.zh_text: 我们已经远远超过了各国领导人承诺坚守的1.5度目标。

blocks.en_text: The Earth has warmed 2 degrees since the 1800s,
blocks.zh_text: 自19世纪以来，地球已经变暖了2度，

blocks.en_text: when the world first started burning fossil fuels in mass scale.
blocks.zh_text: 那时世界首次开始大规模燃烧化石燃料。

blocks.en_text: Reports on heatwaves and wildfires regularly fill the evening news.
blocks.zh_text: 关于热浪和野火的报道经常占据晚间新闻。

blocks.en_text: Summer days exceed 40 degrees in London and 45 degrees in Delhi,
blocks.zh_text: 伦敦的夏日气温超过40度，德里超过45度，

blocks.en_text: as extreme heat waves are now 8 to 9 times more common.
blocks.zh_text: 因为极端热浪现在出现的频率是过去的8到9倍。

blocks.en_text: These high temperatures prompt widespread blackouts,
blocks.zh_text: 这些高温引发了大面积停电，

blocks.en_text: as power grids struggle to keep up with the energy demands
blocks.zh_text: 因为电网难以跟上能源需求

blocks.en_text: needed to properly cool homes.
blocks.zh_text: 而这些能源是给住宅适当降温所必需的。

blocks.en_text: Ambulance sirens blare through the night,
blocks.zh_text: 救护车的警笛声彻夜鸣响，

blocks.en_text: carrying patients suffering from heatstroke, dehydration, and exhaustion.
blocks.zh_text: 运送着中暑、脱水和虚脱的病人。

blocks.en_text: The southwestern United States, southern Africa, and eastern Australia
blocks.zh_text: 美国西南部、非洲南部和澳大利亚东部

blocks.en_text: experience longer, more frequent, and more severe droughts.
blocks.zh_text: 经历着更长、更频繁、更严重的干旱。

blocks.en_text: Meanwhile, the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan
blocks.zh_text: 与此同时，菲律宾、印度尼西亚和日本

blocks.en_text: face more frequent heavy rainfall
blocks.zh_text: 面临更频繁的强降雨

blocks.en_text: as rising temperatures cause water to evaporate faster,
blocks.zh_text: 因为气温上升使水蒸发得更快，

blocks.en_text: and trap more water in the atmosphere.
blocks.zh_text: 并把更多的水困在大气中。

blocks.en_text: As the weather becomes more erratic,
blocks.zh_text: 随着天气变得越来越反复无常，

blocks.en_text: some communities are unable to keep pace with rebuilding
blocks.zh_text: 一些社区无法跟上重建的步伐

blocks.en_text: what’s constantly destroyed.
blocks.zh_text: 去修复不断被摧毁的东西。

blocks.en_text: Many move to cities,
blocks.zh_text: 许多人搬到了城市，

blocks.en_text: where they face housing shortages and a lack of jobs.
blocks.zh_text: 在那里他们面临住房短缺和缺少工作的问题。

blocks.en_text: A resource squeeze is felt in newborn intensive care wards,
blocks.zh_text: 新生儿重症监护病房也感受到了资源紧张，

blocks.en_text: as the rising temperature and air pollution
blocks.zh_text: 因为气温上升和空气污染

blocks.en_text: cause higher rates of premature and underweight births.
blocks.zh_text: 导致早产和低体重婴儿的比例更高。

blocks.en_text: More children develop asthma and respiratory disease,
blocks.zh_text: 更多儿童患上哮喘和呼吸道疾病，

blocks.en_text: and rates balloon in communities regularly exposed to forest fire smoke.
blocks.zh_text: 而在经常暴露于森林火灾烟雾的社区，患病率更是激增。

blocks.en_text: The global emissions added to the atmosphere each year
blocks.zh_text: 每年进入大气层的全球排放量

blocks.en_text: finally start to level off, thanks to government action,
blocks.zh_text: 终于开始趋于平稳，这要归功于政府的行动，

blocks.en_text: but it’s decades too late.
blocks.zh_text: 但这已经晚了几十年。

blocks.en_text: We fail to reach net zero in time.
blocks.zh_text: 我们没能及时实现净零排放。

blocks.en_text: As a result, by 2100 the Earth has warmed another 0.5 to 1.5 degrees.
blocks.zh_text: 结果，到2100年地球又变暖了0.5到1.5度。

blocks.en_text: Over half of our remaining glaciers have melted.
blocks.zh_text: 我们剩余冰川的一半以上已经融化。

blocks.en_text: As the sea heats up, its volume increases due to thermal expansion.
blocks.zh_text: 随着海水变暖，它的体积会因为热膨胀而增大。

blocks.en_text: Together, this elevates sea level by well over a meter.
blocks.zh_text: 两者加在一起，使海平面上升了远超一米。

blocks.en_text: Entire nations, like the Marshall Islands and Tuvalu, are uninhabitable
blocks.zh_text: 像马绍尔群岛和图瓦卢这样的整个国家都变得无法居住，

blocks.en_text: as large swaths of their islands are submerged.
blocks.zh_text: 因为它们岛屿的大片区域被海水淹没了。

blocks.en_text: Some islands, like the Maldives,
blocks.zh_text: 有些岛屿，比如马尔代夫，

blocks.en_text: spend billions building interconnected rafts
blocks.zh_text: 花了几十亿美元建造相互连接的浮筏，

blocks.en_text: that house apartments, schools, and restaurants
blocks.zh_text: 上面有公寓、学校和餐馆，

blocks.en_text: that float above its drowned cities.
blocks.zh_text: 漂浮在被淹没的城市之上。

blocks.en_text: Resettled climate migrants in Jakarta, Mumbai, and Lagos
blocks.zh_text: 在雅加达、孟买和拉各斯重新安置的气候移民

blocks.en_text: are forced to abandon their homes once again,
blocks.zh_text: 被迫再一次放弃他们的家园，

blocks.en_text: as rising tides and extreme storms flood buildings and crumble infrastructure.
blocks.zh_text: 因为上涨的潮水和极端风暴淹没了建筑、摧毁了基础设施。

blocks.en_text: Overall, 250 million people are displaced.
blocks.zh_text: 总体而言，有2.5亿人流离失所。

blocks.en_text: Some affluent cities like New York and Shanghai attempt to adapt,
blocks.zh_text: 一些富裕城市，比如纽约和上海，试图做出调整，

blocks.en_text: elevating buildings and roadways.
blocks.zh_text: 把建筑和道路抬高。

blocks.en_text: Ten-meter-tall seawalls line the cities’ coasts.
blocks.zh_text: 十米高的海堤沿着这些城市的海岸线排开。

blocks.en_text: Children learn about extinct sea life which once inhabited the ocean’s reefs,
blocks.zh_text: 孩子们学习那些曾经栖息在海洋礁石中的已灭绝海洋生物，

blocks.en_text: all of which have vanished thanks to rising surface water temperatures.
blocks.zh_text: 它们全都因为表层水温上升而消失了。

blocks.en_text: Grocery prices skyrocket,
blocks.zh_text: 食品杂货价格飞涨，

blocks.en_text: as food and water scarcity touch all communities.
blocks.zh_text: 因为食物和水资源的短缺波及了所有社区。

blocks.en_text: Fruits and products long grown in the tropics and subtropics
blocks.zh_text: 长期在热带和亚热带种植的水果和产品

blocks.en_text: rarely show up on shelves,
blocks.zh_text: 很少出现在货架上，

blocks.en_text: as intense heat waves paired with increasing humidity
blocks.zh_text: 因为强烈的热浪加上不断增加的湿度

blocks.en_text: make it deadly for farmers to work outdoors.
blocks.zh_text: 让农民在户外劳作变得致命。

blocks.en_text: Unpredictable heatwaves, droughts, and floods
blocks.zh_text: 难以预测的热浪、干旱和洪水

blocks.en_text: cripple small-scale farmers in Africa, Asia, and South America,
blocks.zh_text: 重创了非洲、亚洲和南美洲的小农户，

blocks.en_text: who previously produced one-third of the world’s food.
blocks.zh_text: 他们以前生产了全世界三分之一的粮食。

blocks.en_text: Hundreds of millions of people are pushed into hunger and famine.
blocks.zh_text: 数亿人陷入饥饿和饥荒。

blocks.en_text: Climate predictions can feel overwhelming and terrifying.
blocks.zh_text: 气候预测可能会让人觉得不堪重负、十分可怕。

blocks.en_text: Yet many of the experts responsible for these assessments remain optimistic.
blocks.zh_text: 然而，许多负责这些评估的专家仍然保持乐观。

blocks.en_text: Since countries have first begun taking steps to lower their emissions,
blocks.zh_text: 自从各国首次开始采取措施降低排放以来，

blocks.en_text: warming projections have shifted downwards.
blocks.zh_text: 升温预测已经向下调整。

blocks.en_text: In less than a decade, we’ve reduced our projected emission rates
blocks.zh_text: 在不到十年的时间里，我们降低了预计的排放率，

blocks.en_text: so that we’re no longer on track to hit nearly 4 degrees of warming.
blocks.zh_text: 以至于我们不再朝着接近4摄氏度升温的轨道前进。

blocks.en_text: Policies that invest in renewable energy sources,
blocks.zh_text: 投资可再生能源、

blocks.en_text: cut fossil fuel production, support electric transportation,
blocks.zh_text: 削减化石燃料生产、支持电动交通、

blocks.en_text: protect our forests, and regulate industry
blocks.zh_text: 保护森林以及监管工业的政策

blocks.en_text: can help mitigate the worst effects of climate change.
blocks.zh_text: 可以帮助减轻气候变化最严重的影响。

blocks.en_text: But climate experts have also stressed that current policies and pledges
blocks.zh_text: 但气候专家也强调，目前的政策和承诺

blocks.en_text: don’t go far enough— in speed or scale.
blocks.zh_text: 在速度或规模上都还不够。

blocks.en_text: Enacting real change will require bold solutions,
blocks.zh_text: 要实现真正的改变，需要大胆的解决方案、

blocks.en_text: innovations, and collective action.
blocks.zh_text: 创新和集体行动。

blocks.en_text: There’s still time to rewrite our future, and every tenth of a degree counts.
blocks.zh_text: 我们仍有时间改写未来，而每十分之一度都很重要。
